lens: DaisyUI theme engine: persona-themed skins, user-switchable themes, community themes
name: Signal Skins Console
one_liner: A dark-first coaching console built on daisyUI themes: each sales job gets its own skin, the coaching and scoring colors never change, and skins ship as community-contributable theme files.
lens_followed_or_changed: Followed the DaisyUI theme-engine lens: the theme is the spine. Each sales job (SDR cold call, AE discovery, insurance, solar and so on) is a data-theme skin scoped to its own subtree. Users switch Signal (dark), Ledger (light) or Contrast (AAA). Community skins are PR-able theme files checked in CI. Changed one thing: Second Nature, Hyperbound, Yoodli and Grain compete on live coaching and evidence, not skins. So reserved semantic tokens (amber coach cue, rose objection, teal live, violet AI) are fixed across every skin, and skins only recolor chrome, surfaces and the orb. Self-scores: A look 8, B UX 7, C unique 8, D live coaching 5.3 (conditional on a coach lane shipping), E library and wizard 5.5 (conditional on seeded content), F1 SaaS 6, F2 selling to entities 6 (white-label skin and persona packs for training companies and call centers), F3 not worth it 3.

palette.use: Canvas (dark default); body text on it is about 15:1
Any AI-generated text, model strip and wizard provenance; about 6.8:1 on canvas
Recording, live and listening states; about 9.9:1
Whisper cues and talk-track progress only; about 10.5:1
Objection alerts and the End and grade button; about 6.9:1
Persona skin slot; primary-content is #0B1220 for about 5:1 contrast
Light canvas (keeps the current page background)
Default primary in Ledger; white text about 6.7:1
Cue text on a #FEF3C7 card; about 6.3:1

design_language.typography: Sora 600 and 700 for display (keeps brand continuity). Inter 400, 500 and 600 for UI and body at a 16px base, line-height 1.5. JetBrains Mono 500 for timers, scores and transcript timestamps so numbers do not jitter. Scale 12, 14, 16, 20, 28, 40, 56.
design_language.shape_and_depth: Controls 12px radius, cards 16px, chips fully round. 1px hairlines, almost no drop shadows in dark mode. The active live panel gets a 1px skin-colored ring and an 8% tinted gradient. Header is glass at 80% alpha with 12px blur. The page backdrop is a mesh gradient tinted by the active skin at about 12% opacity.
design_language.motion: Skin change cross-fades colors over 300ms. The whisper cue slides in over 240ms (from the right on desktop, from the bottom on mobile) and collapses to a chip after 12s. Rubric rings ease out over 600ms with a delta badge. Under prefers-reduced-motion the orb becomes a static gradient and all slides become fades.
design_language.iconography: Lucide at 1.75px stroke, 20px in controls. Sales jobs get Lucide glyphs (Phone, ShieldCheck, House, Stethoscope, Car, Briefcase). No emoji anywhere in the product.
design_language.theme_modes: Signal is the default dark mode. Ledger is light and is pinned on the manager view because dense data reads better there. Contrast is an AAA variant of Signal with white base-content and #64748B borders. Persona skins scope through data-theme on the persona's subtree and can be turned off with 'Match persona skin'. Theme choice is saved to the account when signed in and to localStorage otherwise. Every skin is validated for AA text contrast in CI.

navigation_and_ia: Top bar: Practice (home), Library, Create persona, Progress and Team (role-gated). Scenarios and Dashboard are renamed Library and Progress. The theme switcher (three swatches) and the Cmd+K palette sit in the bar. The live call is a focus mode: the header collapses to a skin dot, mono timer and End button, with no nav. Library deep-links per job (/library/sdr, /library/insurance), and facets live in the URL query so a filtered view can be shared. Mobile uses a bottom tab bar (Practice, Library, Create, Progress, More) with a center Start button on Practice; Team sits under More. The demo banner becomes a dismissible strip shown only in demo builds. Every destination is two taps away from anywhere.

live_coaching_and_scoring: Coach lane: a second model call runs beside the persona. It never speaks to the persona and never enters the transcript; cues render as text in the amber card. Output is structured JSON with at most one cue per rep turn, typed as Next question, Objection alert, Talk-track step or Pace warning, each citing the transcript line IDs it used. Scoring: all five criteria re-score after each rep turn (debounced). Each score carries evidence IDs that the debrief reuses, so live and final scores match. Budget: cues under 2s, score deltas under 1s; past budget the UI shows 'thinking' rather than a stale cue. Intensity (Quiet, Balanced, Heavy) caps cue frequency. Self-score D: 5.3, and only conditional on the coach lane and per-turn scoring shipping. The layout alone is about 4.5, because today the screen has no coaching at all.
persona_library_and_wizard: Library: 60+ seeded personas at launch across 12 sales jobs and 14 industries (SDR cold call, AE discovery, B2B procurement, insurance, mortgage, real estate, solar, home services, auto, medical devices, recruiting, retail, customer success, collections). Each persona is a JSON file tagged with job, industry, difficulty, objection types, voice and skin, validated by schema in CI, so a community persona is one pull request. Wizard (open-source core): accepts a job description, product URL, CRM notes, ICP or pasted call; uses OpenAI structured outputs to draft persona, scenario, rubric and talk track in a single schema; every drafted field shows provenance; a 60-second test call gates saving. Self-score E: 5.5 with seeded content. As the app stands today (three built-ins, no wizard) it is about 3.0.
signature_moments: The whole call re-tints to the persona's job skin, while cue and score colors stay fixed, so amber always means coach and rose always means objection.
An amber whisper card with keys 1 and 2 to accept or dismiss, collapsing to a chip after 12 seconds.
Rubric rings on the live rail tick with a delta arrow and an underlined quote when evidence lands.
A debrief moments timeline: click a marker and the exact transcript line is highlighted.
The persona wizard fills its preview card as the model streams the draft, with provenance on hover.
Make a skin: a live contrast checker plus a 'Propose to community' button that opens a pre-filled pull request.
openai_fund_angle: Make the models visible. A model strip on the live call and the debrief names which OpenAI model does each job (coach, grader, wizard) and links to the prompt and token cost. A developer drawer shows the realtime-style event log, borrowed from OpenAI's own playground pattern, so contributors can watch the stream. 'Powered by OpenAI' appears as plain text attribution, not the logo, so the project does not look endorsed. Contributor invitation: personas and skins are small, schema-checked files, so a first pull request is roughly a 10-minute job. 'Add a persona' and 'Make a skin' open pre-filled templates with a live contrast checker. That gives the Codex for Open Source program a real public repo with PR review, maintainer automation and release workflows to show.

inspirations.borrowed: The real-customer-call coaching loop as a gap to design for. This is a vendor claim to verify, not a fact.

implementation.migration_path: Phase 0 (about 1 week): add daisyUI 4.x on the current Tailwind 3 setup, define Signal and Ledger in the Tailwind config, and map existing tokens to daisyUI names so current pages still render. Phase 1: rebuild the live call and the debrief first, since they carry the basic-needs scores. Phase 2: library, wizard and skins, with the theme CI contrast check and persona schema validation. Phase 3: pre-call briefing, progress dashboard and manager view. Phase 4 (optional, after Phase 3): migrate to Tailwind 4 and daisyUI 5, which defines themes in CSS; daisyUI 5 requires Tailwind 4, so the two move together. Keep the old card and btn classes until each screen has moved.

risks: Skin sprawl: each new persona skin adds QA surface. Cap launch at eight skins and gate community skins through a CI contrast check.
A careless community skin could reuse amber, rose, teal or violet as its primary. The validator must reject any skin that does.
daisyUI 5 requires Tailwind 4. Pin daisyUI 4.x until Phase 4 to avoid a mixed-version build.
Without the coach lane the live screen is a skin, not coaching, and the D score falls below 5.0.
Content is the real gate for E: 60 personas take weeks of curation, and wizard drafts need human review before they join the seeded library.
Community personas or skin names could imitate real companies or people. The schema should ban real brand names in persona and skin names.
Dark-first Signal will not suit everyone. Ledger and Contrast must be first-class, and the three.js orb needs a CSS fallback on low-power devices.
Attribution to OpenAI must stay textual and modest so the project does not look endorsed by OpenAI.
